items.title: Why universities are rethinking written exams in the age of AI
items.originalSummary: As generative AI tools become widespread, several universities are piloting oral defenses, in-class essays and project-based portfolios to verify what students have actually learned.
items.learningSummary: As generative AI becomes increasingly prevalent, universities around the world are re-evaluating conventional assessment practices. Traditional written examinations are being scrutinised for their ability to accurately reflect genuine student understanding. In response, several higher education institutions have begun implementing a variety of alternative evaluation methods. These include oral defenses, in-class essays conducted under controlled conditions, and project-based portfolios that showcase sustained academic work over time. Educational leaders maintain that these approaches provide more reliable evidence of what students have genuinely learned and are capable of applying. The shift represents a broader acknowledgement that conventional testing formats may no longer be sufficient to distinguish authentic knowledge from AI-generated responses. This movement is still in its pilot phase at many institutions, though early results suggest heightened student engagement and improved learning outcomes.

readingQuestions.answer: Universities are piloting oral defenses, in-class essays, and project-based portfolios as alternative assessment methods.

readingQuestions.answer: It can be inferred that traditional written examinations may gradually diminish in importance as institutions seek more reliable methods to confirm genuine student learning, especially given the rise of AI tools.

items.writingPrompt: In recent years, artificial intelligence has become accessible to students at an unprecedented scale. As a result, some universities are replacing traditional written examinations with oral defenses, essays written in class, and project portfolios. Do you think this shift in assessment methods is a positive development for education? Give reasons for your answer and include relevant examples from your knowledge or experience.
items.listeningText: The widespread availability of generative artificial intelligence is prompting a fundamental rethink of how universities assess student performance. For decades, written examinations served as the primary method for evaluating academic achievement. However, educators now face the challenge of distinguishing between work produced by students themselves and content generated by AI tools. In response, numerous institutions have begun experimenting with alternative assessment formats. Oral defenses allow examiners to question students directly, making it far more difficult to present someone else's work as one's own. In-class essays, completed under supervision, offer a middle ground between flexibility and integrity. Meanwhile, project portfolios enable students to demonstrate learning over an extended period. While these approaches are still being refined, many academics believe they more accurately reflect genuine understanding and critical thinking skills.

items.title: Why universities are rethinking written exams in the age of AI
items.originalSummary: As generative AI tools become widespread, several universities are piloting oral defenses, in-class essays and project-based portfolios to verify what students have actually learned.
items.learningSummary: Universities around the world are experimenting with new assessment formats as the use of generative AI tools spreads on campus. Instead of relying solely on take-home essays, some institutions are introducing oral defenses, in-class writing tasks and project-based portfolios that are harder to outsource. Supporters argue these methods give a more reliable picture of a student's real ability, while critics warn that they can be time-consuming and stressful for both students and staff. Educators broadly agree that the goal is not to ban technology but to redesign tasks so that AI becomes a study aid rather than a shortcut.

items.writingPrompt: Some people think universities should redesign assessments because of generative AI, while others believe traditional written exams remain the fairest test. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
items.listeningText: Universities are quietly rethinking how they assess their students. With generative AI now widely available, take-home essays no longer prove what a student really understands. As a response, several institutions are piloting oral defenses, timed in-class writing and small group projects. Supporters say these formats offer a more reliable view of student learning, especially when combined with regular feedback. Critics, however, point out that they take more time to mark and can feel stressful for those who are not confident speakers. Most educators agree on one thing: the aim is not to fight technology, but to redesign assessments so that AI supports learning instead of replacing it.
